## Design

### 2026-10-06 – Just got started working on my first project for half life. I decided to create a project I've wanted for a while, which is an uninterruptable power supply module board. With my battery powered electr

**3h**

Just got started working on my first project for half life. I decided to create a project I've wanted for a while, which is an uninterruptable power supply module board. With my battery powered electronics projects I often want it to be rechargeable and usable while charging, which isn't very simple to do. This product that already sortof exists, the PowerBoost 1000 charger.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 214141](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/49dfe2e366c7c89c81cdbc70982b3cb0150b1f45992805a283c1f26e5db1010b.png)

However, this thing is kinda expensive, uses micro usb, and only supports 1 amp of power output, so you wouldn't be able to use this to power a a raspberry pi for example.

I spent some time researching parts that would allow for higher current and I am thinking the TPS61089 should work for the boost convertor, but I'm still not sure what to use for the actual battery charger/load balancer.

It's nice that adafruit's designs are open source so I know what this thing is even supposed to look like. I'm still fairly inexperienced in electronics beyond basic led's and resistors. I've learned about logic gates but thats not very helpful here lol. I spent some time looking at its schematics and trying to understand on a high level how a device like this works.

I started a new kicad project and added usb c for power input and a USB A for power out because thats what the PowerBoost 1000 does, but I'm not sure I actually want that now. I may just have a couple power pads that you can connect to anything.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 205044](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/7c65a5f4d30b5cfc1f38c27f47cf1670cad1c100b7ef9ce33a7e358ec8c95b1a.png)

I also started messing with the TPS61089 and started wiring it according to the datasheet's typical use example while trying to understand what each part is for. I haven't figured out what values to put for all the capacitors and programming resistors yet, which is what I'm gonna work on next time

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 210858](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/508d14ffa26bf0ce5f62f8f028cd9059703f2a9e9fe8e5318b8520e1a41b0064.png)

TLDR; I'm making a better version of the adafruit powerboost 1000c. Started a new kicad project and started deciding wiring components

### 2026-10-10 – Today I locked in and finished and finished my entire schematic design, so now I pretty much just have to assign footprints and route the board.

**4h**

Today I locked in and finished and finished my entire schematic design, so now I pretty much just have to assign footprints and route the board.

When I left off I still hadn't figured out which battery charging circuit I wanted to use. The powerboost 1000c uses the MCP73871, but it only supports an output of 2 amps. Ideally I wanted to be able to output 4 or 5 amps, but chips with that capability required i^2 c programming which would add way too much complexity and I am running out of time. I also looked into some simple methods that just use diodes and a couple of mosfets combined with a standard charging ic like the tp4056. The article I read about it said it wouldn't handle gracefully if I overload the input power supply, so I decided  to go with something else

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 132925](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/c365b5dcc1b6f50ddcccf98db6c62f1a615c59567889fb6f3b5cc6b1850c2bbb.png)

The best I could find was the texas instruments BQ25306. It can output 3 amps, which should be able to power up to like a raspberry pi 4, as long as the battery or input supply can deliver that amount.

I made a snap eda account so I could download the schematic and footprint and import it to kicad. I began wiring up the basic connections by following the typical application with external power path guide, and ignored it for the time when It didn't provide a value for the component for me

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 121212](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/21aeacb8cdd36e55229dd7296319e33c6095316857af6a93c2d50effb0deae3e.png)

This time was a bit more straightforward than the boost converter. I still have no idea what some of those capacitors are doing in the boost convertor, but with this one I feel like I was able to get a good understanding of what each part does and the reasoning of its value by reading the datasheet. this table was especially useful.
![Screenshot 2026-10-10 134553](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/06eb94b3672362de8f0b4940a0026507d65a2a8197c3add5122330bbcf290446.png)

I decided to not implement the thermosistor pin because not all batteries have them so hopefully that isn't an issue. I assume it will just make it so that their is no tempurature based battery protection and  I guess I'm fine with that.

I finally finished up everything specific to the battery charger ic, and hooked it up to the boost convertor. It works essentially the same way as the powerboost, just with different integrated circuits. so in theory If I configured them correctly, my design should be functional. I also decided to scrap the usb A connector and I'm just using two header pins that you'll be able connect anywhere. Up next, I just have to assign footprints to each component and I can start creating the board. but the theoretical circuit design is complete!

![[Screenshot 2026-10-10 123511.png]]

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 123511](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/874ed43a3568ab3b3bbb9f7dda2cb114e5f3d2a2579d6ebb0fc44f56ade1e6c4.png)

TLDR; I researched and implemented everything to do with the battery charging using a BQ25306, my design is complete and I finalized my circuit schematic.
